root_cause: The Govuk radios component only updates ARIA attributes and conditional visibility on click events. Keyboard arrow navigation changes the checked state of radio buttons without firing a click event, so the associated conditional content remains visible when it should be hidden.
repair_strategy: Add a 'change' event listener to the radios module that invokes the same attribute-update logic as the click handler, ensuring that any change to a radio's checked state (whether via mouse, keyboard, or other input) correctly shows or hides its associated conditional content.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation via arrow keys will now correctly show or hide conditional fields, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Both click and change events may fire for the same user interaction, causing duplicate attribute updates; however, the outcome is idempotent and harmless.
The change listener will only affect radio inputs that have an aria-controls attribute, leaving other form controls unaffected.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Text message radio hides the mobile number field when moving to the opt-out radio.
Verify that pressing ArrowUp from the opt-out radio shows the mobile number field when moving back to the Text message radio.
Verify that mouse clicks on radios continue to show/hide conditionals correctly.
Verify that the existing regression guard (choose email via keyboard and enter address) still passes.
Verify that form data reflects the selected radio value after keyboard navigation.
